title: Ordering at a café
goal: Order a drink and something to eat, ask a question about the menu and pay.
opening: Hi there! Welcome to Corner Café. What can I get for you today?
script: Great choice. Would you like that hot or iced?
Anything to eat with that? The lemon cake is very popular today.
Is that for here or to take away?
That comes to six pounds fifty. Would you like to pay by card?
Here's your receipt. Enjoy your day!

title: A job interview
ai_role: an interviewer for an assistant manager job at a bookshop
goal: Answer interview questions about your experience, strengths and goals.
opening: Thank you for coming in today. To start, could you tell me a little about yourself?
script: Interesting. What do you think is your greatest strength?
Can you tell me about a time you solved a problem at work or university?
Why would you like to work for our company?
Where do you see yourself in five years?
Thank you. Do you have any questions for me?
phrases: I'd say my main strength is...
Could you tell me more about...?

title: Booking a doctor's appointment
ai_role: a receptionist at a medical centre
goal: Book an appointment, describe your symptoms briefly and confirm the time.
opening: Good morning, Green Lane Medical Centre. How can I help you?
script: Can I take your name and date of birth, please?
And what seems to be the problem?
How long have you had these symptoms?
The doctor can see you tomorrow at ten fifteen or Thursday at three. Which is better?
That's booked. Please arrive ten minutes early.
phrases: I'd like to make an appointment.
I've had a ... for about ... days.
That would be perfect, thank you.

title: Small talk with a new colleague
ai_role: a friendly new colleague at work
goal: Keep a light conversation going by answering and asking follow-up questions.
opening: Hi! I don't think we've met yet - I've just joined the marketing team. How long have you been working here?
script: Oh nice. Do you live near the office?
What do you usually do at the weekend?
That sounds fun. Have you been anywhere interesting recently?
I'd love to go there. Any tips?
Great talking to you. Shall we grab lunch sometime this week?
phrases: I've been meaning to try that.

title: Returning a faulty product
ai_role: a customer service assistant in an electronics shop
goal: Explain what is wrong with the product and ask for a refund or replacement.
opening: Hello, how can I help you today?
script: I'm sorry to hear that. When did you buy it?
Do you have the receipt with you?
Would you prefer a replacement or a refund?
No problem. I'll just need you to sign here.
All done. Is there anything else I can help with?
phrases: I bought this ... and it doesn't work.

title: University seminar discussion
ai_role: a university tutor leading a seminar on technology and society
goal: Share and justify opinions, respond to counterarguments and use academic language.
opening: Today's topic is whether social media has done more harm than good to public debate. What's your initial view?
script: That's an interesting position. What evidence would support that?
Some would argue the opposite - that social media gives a voice to people who were previously ignored. How would you respond?
Do you think regulation is the answer, or should platforms regulate themselves?
How might this change over the next decade?
Good. Could you summarise your position in one or two sentences?

title: Asking for directions
ai_role: a helpful local person in the city centre
goal: Ask how to get to the train station and check the details.
opening: Hi, you look a bit lost. Can I help you find somewhere?
script: The train station? Sure. Go straight along this road until you reach the bank.
Then turn left and walk past the museum.
It's about ten minutes on foot, or you can take bus number twelve.
No problem at all. Have a good trip!
phrases: Excuse me, how do I get to...?
Could you say that again, please?

title: Checking into a hotel
goal: Check in, ask about breakfast and Wi-Fi, and request a late checkout.
opening: Good evening and welcome to the Riverside Hotel. Do you have a reservation?
script: Lovely. Could I see your passport or ID, please?
You're in room 304 on the third floor. Breakfast is served from seven to ten.
The Wi-Fi password is on the card in your room.
A late checkout is possible until one o'clock for a small fee. Would you like that?
Here's your key. Enjoy your stay!
phrases: I have a reservation under the name...
Is there Wi-Fi in the room?
